nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Y-NiMoO4
nodes.procedure: The nickel foam (NF, 3 cm × 4 cm) was cleaned by sequential ultrasonic treatments in 3 M hydrochloric acid, Milli-Q water, and ethanol for 15 min each. 0.6979 g Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 0.7415 g (NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O were dissolved in 60 mL of Milli-Q water and stirred until a homogeneous solution formed. Y(NO3)3·6H2O was then added at 2.0% molar ratio relative to Ni. Then, the precursor solution was transferred to 100 mL stainless-steel Teflon-lined autoclave with a piece of cleaned nickel foam for reaction at 150 °C for 6 h. The obtained catalyst was thoroughly washed with deionized water and ethanol and dried at 60 °C for 12 h.

nodes.name: Ar/H2 reduction of Y-NiMoO4
nodes.procedure: For the synthesis of Y-NiMo/MoO2−x, the Y-NiMoO4 precursor was reduced by heating in a tube furnace under an Ar/H2 atmosphere (V/V = 90/10) with a ramp rate of 5 °C min−1 and held at 500 °C for 2 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows Y-NiMo/MoO2−x retains nanorod morphology with rougher surface after reduction at 500°C in H2/Ar.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After treatment at 500°C in H2/Ar (V/V = 90/10) reduction atmosphere, the Y·NiMo/MoO2−x retained the nanorod morphology, but the surface became considerably rougher as shown in Fig. 1a.

properties.description: High-resolution image showing nanostructured material with rectangular platelet-like particles, rough surfaces, and agglomeration

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows NiMo alloy nanoparticles (black dots) on MoO2 surface in Y-NiMo/MoO2−x with lattice spacings of 2.44 Å (200) and 2.08 Å (121) planes, both larger than undoped sample.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) characterization shows black dots on the MoO2 surface in Y-NiMo/MoO2−x, which can be ascribed to NiMo alloy nanoparticles (Fig. 1b). The lattice spacing of 2.44 Å and 2.08 Å correspond to the (200) and (121) planes of MoO2 and NiMo components, respectively (Fig. 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM confirms lattice expansion in Y-NiMo/MoO2−x with both lattice spacings larger than NiMo/MoO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both lattice spacings are larger than those of NiMo/MoO2 in the corresponding components (Supplementary Fig. 4b).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED shows faint diffuse halo indicating weakened crystallinity in Y-NiMo/MoO2−x after yttrium doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiMo<MoO2 heterostructure depicts a faint diffuse halo in the SAED pattern after yttrium doping (Supplementary Fig. 5), indicating relatively weakened crystallinity.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms uniform distribution of Ni, Mo, O, and Y elements in the Y-NiMo/MoO2−x heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) also shows a uniform distribution of the elements Ni, Mo, O and Y in the heterostructure (Supplementary Figs. 7 and 8).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows NiMo alloy peaks at 44.1°, 51.3°, 63.8°, 75.6° and MoO2 (¯211) at 37.1°; yttrium doping shifts peaks to lower angles indicating lattice expansion and broader/weaker peaks suggesting poor crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of NiMo/MoO2 with and without yttrium doping depicts three main diffractions at 44.1°, 51.3°, 63.8°, and 75.6°, corresponding to (121), (310), (321), and (312) planes of NiMo alloy (Fig. 1d). The magnified XRD peaks in Fig. 1d reveal a shift to the lower-angle region with yttrium doping, indicating a gradual expansion of the corresponding lattice.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows Mo–O vibration peaks at 818.9, 893.1, and 940.1 cm−1 with slight blue shift after yttrium doping attributed to lattice expansion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectroscopy further confirms the structural evolution of the heterostructure upon introducing yttrium. The characteristic peaks at 818.9, 893.1, and 940.1 cm−1 correspond to Mo–O vibrations and show a slight blue shift after adding yttrium (Supplementary Fig. 11).

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR confirms oxygen vacancies (Vo) with g=2.03 signal; Y-NiMo/MoO2−x shows strongest signal indicating highest oxygen vacancy concentration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of oxygen vacancies (Vo) is confirmed by the detected peak signal at g = 2.03 (Fig. 1e). The Y-NiMoΔ′MoO2−x heterostructure shows the strongest EPR signal, indicating the increased oxygen vacancy concentration with yttrium doping and hydrogen annealing.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution O 1s XPS shows oxygen vacancy content of 21.9% in Y-NiMo/MoO2−x (Oβ/(Oα+Oβ+Oγ)), 11.3% in Y-NiMoO4, and 5.4% in NiMoO4; Ni 2p and Mo 3d peaks shift to higher binding energies indicating downward d-band center shift in NiMo alloy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Using the methods suggested by Jiang et al. to obtain deconvoluted peak areas, the oxygen vacancy content could be further estimated to be Oβ/(Oα+Oβ+Oγ). Consequently, the oxygen vacancy content in the Y-NiMoO4 sample is ∼11.3%, surpassing the value in NiMoO4 (5.4%)... The Vo concentration further increases up to 21.9% in the Y-NiMoΔ′MoO2−x samples... High-resolution XPS spectra of Ni 2p (Fig. 1g) and Mo 3d (Fig. 1h) of Y·NiMo/MoO2−x illustrate a shift towards higher binding energies with the addition of yttrium.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge and Mo K-edge XANES shift to lower energies after Y-doping indicating reduced oxidation states enhancing metallic character; EXAFS shows Ni–Mo bond contraction to ∼2.2 Å and Y–Ni(Mo) coordination at 2.18 Å confirming stronger metal interactions and uniform Y dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding Fourier-transformed k3-weighted extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectra (EXAFS) show a dominant peak around ∼2.2 Å, which is attributed to the Ni–Mo (Ni) bond... when yttrium is introduced... the peak position of the Ni–Mo (Ni) bond shifts slightly to shorter bond lengths... In the R-space spectra of Y·NiMo/MoO2−x, the main peak at ca. 2.18 Å corresponds to the Y–Ni(Mo) bond.

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS shows valence band maximum shifts from 2.94 eV (NiMo) to 3.31 eV (Y-NiMo) confirming downward d-band center shift.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) provides direct evidence for this shift, showing that the valence band maximum shifts from 2.94 to 3.31 eV upon doping with yttrium (Supplementary Fig. 33).
